voiceover: It's 2am, you type git commit, and git quietly saves a snapshot of your whole project. Not just your changes. Everything. Every commit records what every file in your project looked like at that moment. Git is clever, though: each file's content gets a hash, a fingerprint, and identical content is stored only once. If a file didn't change, the new commit just points to the copy git already has. Each commit also stores the hash of the commit before it, so history is a chain. Change anything old and every hash after it changes too. When git shows you a diff, it's comparing two snapshots on the spot. Part two: what a branch really is.
